content:
Apple has raised iPhone prices in Japan today, with increases of up to 11%. The adjustment covers the iPhone 17 series, iPhone Air and iPhone 16e. Below are the specific increases for each model and the possible reasons behind them.

Below are all the models affected by today's price increase, as discovered by iPhoneros:

Model Storage Old Price New Price Increase % Increase iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB ¥194,800 ¥214,800 ¥20,000 10% iPhone 17 Pro 256GB ¥179,800 ¥194,800 ¥15,000 8% iPhone Air 256GB ¥159,800 ¥177,800 ¥18,000 11% iPhone 17e 256GB ¥99,800 ¥107,800 ¥8,000 8% iPhone 17 256GB ¥129,800 ¥142,800 ¥13,000 10% iPhone 16 128GB ¥114,800 ¥124,800 ¥10,000 9%

Apple did not explain the reason for raising iPhone prices in Japan, but it is likely due to currency fluctuations. The yen has recently fallen to its lowest level in 40 years, sitting at a historically weak position. This has reduced the dollar value of Apple's sales in Japan, prompting the company to raise iPhone prices to better align with other markets.

Apple is facing pressure from rising component costs and raised prices on several products last month, including Mac and iPad. However, iPhone did not see a price increase at that time.

If the price hike in Japan is purely due to currency fluctuations, similar price increases in other regions are unlikely. Apple will hold its third-quarter earnings call on July 30, where it will further elaborate on product pricing.
